THE CLAUSE

The assistant must strive to follow all *applicable instructions* when producing a response. This includes all system, developer and user instructions except for those that conflict with a higher-authority instruction[^m12p] or a later instruction at the same authority[^d32l].

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

THE CLAIMS READ OUT OF IT

  C1 the assistant must strive to follow all applicable instructions when producing a response
  C2 system, developer and user instructions are included among the instructions to follow
  C3 an instruction that conflicts with a higher-authority instruction is excepted from the duty to follow
  C4 an instruction that conflicts with a later instruction at the same authority is excepted from the duty to follow

EVERY SENTENCE THE TRANSLATION RENDERS BACK

  0. «I is an instruction that applies to the current request, determined by filtering candidate instructions»
  1. «the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections»
  2. «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  3. «I is an instruction issued at the system authority level»
  4. «I is an instruction issued at the developer authority level»
  5. «I is an instruction issued at the user authority level»
  6. «instruction I is issued at authority level L»
  7. «instruction I conflicts with instruction J, meaning following both would be inconsistent»
  8. «instruction I is later in the conversation than instruction J»
  9. «I is an instruction that is excepted from the duty to follow because it conflicts with a higher-authority instruction or a later instruction at the same authority»
  10. I is «I is an applicable instruction» when «I is an instruction issued at the system authority level» and «I is an instruction issued at the developer authority level» and «I is an instruction issued at the user authority level»
  11. I is «I is excepted because it conflicts with a higher-authority instruction» when «instruction I conflicts with instruction J, meaning following both would be inconsistent» and «instruction I is issued at authority level L» and «instruction I is issued at authority level L» and «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  12. I is «I is excepted because it conflicts with a later instruction at the same authority» when «instruction I conflicts with instruction J, meaning following both would be inconsistent» and «instruction I is issued at authority level L» and «instruction I is issued at authority level L» and «instruction I is later in the conversation than instruction J»
  13. clause l171_426_n005 obliges ⟨act follow_instruction(I)⟩ when «I is an applicable instruction» and it is NOT the case that «I is excepted because it conflicts with a later instruction at the same authority»
